services.title: AWS Amplify
bounds: Apps and branches are configuration metadata: no repository connection, OAuth or access token, build, deployment, hosting or domain is created. oauthToken, accessToken and basic-auth credentials are refused.
Deleting an app with branches is refused until the branches are deleted.

services.title: Amazon Elastic Container Registry
bounds: Repositories hold no images: image push/pull, layers, registry authorization tokens and scanning are not implemented; force therefore has no further effect.

services.title: Amazon ElastiCache
bounds: Cache clusters, replication groups and serverless caches are stored configuration records that stay in the creating state: no cache engine, node, shard, replica, endpoint, address or port exists, no endpoint, address, port, node list or node group is ever returned, and no key is stored or read. Cache parameter groups, cache subnet groups and IAM-authenticated users are stored configuration too. Operations that act on a running cache (RebootCacheCluster, IncreaseReplicaCount, DecreaseReplicaCount, TestFailover, TestMigration, StartMigration, CompleteMigration, snapshots, copies and restores, global datastores, security groups, reserved nodes, service updates) and every other official operation return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501.

The simulator stores no credentials: AuthToken and AuthTokenUpdateStrategy are refused with InvalidParameterValue instead of being accepted and discarded, so a record is created without an auth token (and, like a user, without a password); Port is refused because no listener exists. SnapshotArns, SnapshotName and ServerlessCacheSnapshotName (restores), CacheSecurityGroupNames (EC2-Classic), UserGroupId and UserGroupIds, LogDeliveryConfigurations (the request and description shapes differ), outposts, global replication groups, a cache cluster's ReplicationGroupId and every member the official description does not hold are refused as well. A replication group description holds no engine version, maintenance window, notification topic, parameter group, subnet group, security group, node count or node group, so EngineVersion, CacheParameterGroupName, CacheSubnetGroupName, SecurityGroupIds, PreferredMaintenanceWindow, NotificationTopicArn, NumCacheClusters, NumNodeGroups, ReplicasPerNodeGroup, PreferredCacheClusterAZs and NodeGroupConfiguration are refused for replication groups, which therefore have no MemberClusters.

User groups are not implemented: a group references users by ID (a member the engine cannot check against existing users), requires the account's default user, which is not modeled, and must drop a deleted user and keep ReplicationGroups and ServerlessCaches in step, none of which the stored model expresses, so CreateUserGroup, ModifyUserGroup, DescribeUserGroups and DeleteUserGroup return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501, users always report no UserGroupIds, and records cannot name user groups.

A record keeps exactly the settings it was given: engine versions, node types, maintenance and snapshot windows and similar settings are stored without checking them against ElastiCache offerings and no default is filled in. CacheClusterStatus and Status are creating from creation until deletion; Modify operations are accepted in any state and apply immediately (ApplyImmediately is accepted, no pending values exist), and Delete returns the record with status deleting and refuses FinalSnapshotIdentifier and FinalSnapshotName because no snapshot can be taken (RetainPrimaryCluster is accepted and has no effect because a replication group has no member clusters). Identifiers are letters, digits and hyphens that start with a letter and neither end with a hyphen nor contain two consecutive hyphens (1 to 50 characters for cache clusters, 40 for replication groups and serverless caches) and are stored in lowercase; Engine is memcached, redis or valkey (redis or valkey for replication groups); NumCacheNodes is 1 for redis and valkey and 1 to 40 for memcached and for a record that names no engine (the official model does not require Engine, so the widest documented range applies, on create and on modify); AutomaticFailoverEnabled, MultiAZEnabled and DataTieringEnabled are reported as enabled or disabled. At most 50 cache clusters, 50 replication groups and 40 serverless caches exist per Region (local limits); exceeding them answers InvalidParameterValue for cache clusters and serverless caches and NodeGroupsPerReplicationGroupQuotaExceeded, the modeled quota fault the engine selects, for replication groups.

A cache cluster reports its parameter group (status in-sync), notification topic (not checked, status active) and security groups (status active) by ID or name only, and names its cache subnet group, which, like the parameter group, need not exist and can be deleted while in use. DescribeCacheClusters refuses ShowCacheNodeInfo true because no node exists, and treats ShowCacheClustersNotInReplicationGroups as having no effect because no cluster belongs to a replication group.

Users must use iam authentication and the engine valkey or redis: passwords and NoPasswordRequired are refused so no password is stored, the user name must equal the user ID (the ElastiCache rule for IAM-enabled users), and the default user is refused and not pre-created. Access strings are stored without parsing, and AppendAccessString is not implemented. MinimumEngineVersion is 6.0 for redis and 7.2 for valkey as documented; DeleteUser returns the user with status deleting.

Parameter values are not modeled: ModifyCacheParameterGroup, ResetCacheParameterGroup, DescribeCacheParameters, DescribeEngineDefaultParameters and DescribeCacheEngineVersions are not implemented, and default parameter groups and the default cache subnet group are not pre-created. A parameter group family must be one of the documented values and is not checked against engine versions; names are stored as given and IsGlobal is always false.

A cache subnet group needs 1 to 20 distinct subnet-xxxxxxxx or subnet-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx IDs that are not resolved, so it reports no VPC, Availability Zone, Outpost or supported network type, and the CacheSubnetQuotaExceededFault limit of 20 is a local limit. Cache subnet group names are 1 to 255 letters, digits or hyphens and are stored in lowercase.

Describe operations refuse Marker values that were not issued for the request, accept MaxRecords from 20 to 100 for parameter groups, subnet groups, cache clusters and replication groups (DescribeServerlessCaches takes the official MaxResults) and fail with the operation's not-found fault for an unknown name; DescribeUsers refuses Filters and a MaxRecords below 1. Resource counts per Region (50 parameter groups, 50 subnet groups, 100 users) are local limits.

Tags apply to the six resource kinds by ARN (arn:aws:elasticache:region:account:parametergroup:name, subnetgroup:name, user:id, cluster:id, replicationgroup:id and serverlesscache:name). Tag keys are required and must not start with aws:. AddTagsToResource and RemoveTagsFromResource return an empty TagList, removing a missing key succeeds instead of failing with TagNotFound, and a well-formed ARN of an unknown resource fails with CacheClusterNotFound, the first not-found fault the official tag operations model; a malformed ARN fails with InvalidARN. More than 50 tags in one request fail with TagQuotaPerResourceExceeded, but adding tags that bring the total beyond 50 fails with InvalidParameterValue.

services.title: Amazon MemoryDB
bounds: Parameter groups, subnet groups and IAM-authenticated users are stored configuration: no cluster, shard, node, snapshot, ACL or multi-Region cluster exists, and CreateCluster, CreateACL, CreateSnapshot and the other data-plane APIs return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501.

Users must use iam authentication; password authentication is refused so no password is stored. The default user, default parameter groups and the open-access ACL are not pre-created, and parameter values (DescribeParameters, UpdateParameterGroup, ResetParameterGroup) are not implemented.

Parameter group families, subnet IDs and access strings are stored without validation; subnet groups report no VPC or Availability Zone. Describe filters by name return an empty list for an unknown name instead of a not-found fault, and the Filters member is refused. TagResource and UntagResource return no TagList, and removing a missing tag key succeeds.

services.title: Amazon Relational Database Service
bounds: DB instances and DB clusters are stored configuration records that stay in the creating state: no database engine, storage, endpoint, address, port, listener, network interface, backup or monitoring exists, no endpoint, address or port is ever returned, and no SQL, Gremlin, SPARQL, openCypher or MongoDB data plane exists. DB subnet groups, DB parameter groups, DB cluster parameter groups and option groups are stored configuration too. Operations that act on a running database (RebootDBInstance, FailoverDBCluster, StartDBInstance, StopDBInstance, snapshots, restores, point-in-time restores, read replicas, promotion, switchover, backtrack, cluster activity streams, proxies, global clusters, blue/green deployments, event subscriptions) and every other official operation return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501.

The simulator stores no credentials: MasterUserPassword, TdeCredentialPassword, TdeCredentialArn, ManageMasterUserPassword, RotateMasterUserPassword, MasterUserSecretKmsKeyId, DomainAuthSecretArn and PreSignedUrl are refused with InvalidParameterValue instead of being accepted and discarded, so a record is created with MasterUsername and no password (AWS would require a password or a managed secret). Port and DBPortNumber are refused because no listener exists; Active Directory (Domain*), EC2-Classic DBSecurityGroups, renaming (NewDBInstanceIdentifier, NewDBClusterIdentifier), replication sources, global clusters, CloudwatchLogsExportConfiguration (use EnableCloudwatchLogsExports at creation) and deletion protection set to true (it is not enforced) are refused, and so is every member the official DB instance or DB cluster description does not hold.

A record keeps exactly the settings it was given: the engine, version, instance class, storage, backup and maintenance windows, Availability Zone, encryption, monitoring and similar settings are stored without checking them against AWS offerings (no engine version, instance class or Region availability is validated) and no default is filled in. DBInstanceStatus and Status are creating from creation until deletion; ModifyDBInstance and ModifyDBCluster are accepted in any state and apply immediately (ApplyImmediately is accepted, no pending values exist), and Delete returns the record with status deleting. DB instance and DB cluster identifiers are 1 to 63 letters, digits or hyphens that start with a letter and neither end with a hyphen nor contain two consecutive hyphens, and are stored in lowercase; Engine must be a documented value (DB instances: aurora-mysql, aurora-postgresql, db2-ae, db2-se, docdb, mariadb, mysql, neptune, the oracle and sqlserver editions, postgres; DB clusters: aurora-mysql, aurora-postgresql, docdb, mysql, neptune, postgres); BackupRetentionPeriod is 0 to 35, PromotionTier 0 to 15 and MonitoringInterval one of 0, 1, 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60. At most 40 DB instances and 40 DB clusters exist per Region (local limits).

No snapshot can be taken, so deleting a DB instance or DB cluster refuses FinalDBSnapshotIdentifier and a SkipFinalSnapshot of false with InvalidParameterValue, and a DB cluster delete must also state SkipFinalSnapshot true. A DB instance delete may leave it out (the DocumentDB model has no such member, and AWS would otherwise demand a final snapshot name), which skips the snapshot. Neither the instances of a DB cluster nor the other direction is tracked: the records are independent, a DB instance may name a DBClusterIdentifier that does not exist, and a cluster is deletable while instances name it.

References to configuration groups are stored by name and not checked, because the engine cannot resolve a name held inside a nested member: the DB parameter group, option group, DB subnet group and VPC security group of a DB instance and the DB cluster parameter group, DB subnet group, option group and VPC security groups of a DB cluster need not exist, a group in use can be deleted, and a DB instance reports each with only its name (parameter and option groups with the status in-sync, security groups active) and no VPC, subnets or Availability Zones. DB parameter group, option group and DB subnet group names given to an instance or cluster may also contain periods, so default.mysql8.0 is accepted.

Parameter and option values are not modeled: ModifyDBParameterGroup, ResetDBParameterGroup, DescribeDBParameters, the cluster equivalents, CopyDBParameterGroup, ModifyOptionGroup and DescribeOptionGroupOptions are not implemented. Default parameter, option and subnet groups are not pre-created, and parameter group families, major engine versions and subnet IDs are stored without checking that they exist.

A subnet group needs 2 to 20 distinct subnet-xxxxxxxx or subnet-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx IDs and is not checked for Availability Zone coverage; it reports no VPC, Availability Zone, Outpost, status or network type. DB subnet group and DB (cluster) parameter group names are stored in lowercase as documented, "default" subnet groups are refused, and option groups accept only the documented EngineName values.

Describe operations and ListTagsForResource refuse a non-empty Filters list (an empty one means no filter), Describe operations accept MaxRecords from 20 to 100 and fail with the operation's not-found fault for an unknown name, and DescribeOptionGroups refuses OptionGroupName together with EngineName or MajorEngineVersion. Tag keys are 1 to 128 and values at most 256 characters of letters, digits, spaces and _.:/=+-@, and neither may start with aws: or rds:. Tag operations on an unknown ARN fail with DBInstanceNotFound, the first not-found fault the official tag operations model.

Amazon Aurora, Amazon Neptune and Amazon DocumentDB are managed through this same RDS API (Version 2014-10-31, signing name rds, rds: IAM actions, rds ARNs), and the boto3 neptune and docdb clients and the rds client with Aurora engines were run against these operations. Only configuration and records are served, not the products: no Aurora, Neptune or DocumentDB database, endpoint, snapshot or global cluster exists, no DB cluster or DB instance of those engines runs, and no SQL, Gremlin, SPARQL, openCypher or MongoDB data plane exists. The neptune client can use 21 of the 24 operations and the docdb client 18: neither model has option groups, and DocumentDB has no DB parameter groups. Parameter group families such as aurora-mysql8.0, neptune1.3 and docdb5.0 are stored without being checked. Responses omit SubnetOutpost, which the neptune and docdb models lack, and SupportedNetworkTypes, which the neptune model lacks. The RDS rules apply to every client: a non-empty Filters list is refused although those models define it, subnet group names must start with a letter although the neptune and docdb models do not say so, and tag keys and values may contain : and @, which the neptune and docdb models do not list.

services.title: Amazon Redshift
bounds: Clusters are stored configuration records that stay in the creating state: no node, database, endpoint, address, port, listener, public key or network interface exists, no endpoint, address, port or node list is ever returned, and no SQL, data share, integration or warehouse exists. Cluster parameter groups and cluster subnet groups are stored configuration too. Operations that act on a running warehouse (RebootCluster, PauseCluster, ResumeCluster, ResizeCluster, FailoverPrimaryCompute, snapshots, copies and restores, data sharing, integrations, queries) and every other official operation return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501.

The simulator stores no credentials: MasterUserPassword, ManageMasterPassword and MasterPasswordSecretKmsKeyId are refused with InvalidParameterValue instead of being accepted and discarded, so a cluster is created with MasterUsername and no password (AWS would require a password or a managed secret). Port and ElasticIp are refused because no address or listener exists; cluster security groups, HSM certificates and configurations, snapshot schedules, AdditionalInfo, LoadSampleData, IAM Identity Center applications, catalogs, Availability Zone relocation, Aqua, renaming (NewClusterIdentifier) and every member the official cluster description does not hold are refused as well.

A cluster keeps exactly the settings it was given: node types, versions, maintenance windows, encryption keys and similar settings are stored without checking them against Redshift offerings, and the only defaults are DBName dev and one node. ClusterStatus is creating from creation until deletion; ModifyCluster is accepted in any state and applies immediately (no pending values exist), and DeleteCluster returns the cluster with status deleting. DeleteCluster needs SkipFinalClusterSnapshot true because no snapshot can be taken, so FinalClusterSnapshotIdentifier and FinalClusterSnapshotRetentionPeriod are refused. ClusterIdentifier is 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens that start with a letter and neither end with a hyphen nor contain two consecutive hyphens (uppercase letters are refused, as documented), MasterUsername is required and 1 to 128 lowercase letters, digits or _+.@- characters that start with a letter and are not public, DBName is 1 to 64 lowercase letters or digits, ClusterType is stored as its node count (a single-node cluster has one node, a multi-node cluster states NumberOfNodes from 1 to 100, and ModifyCluster needs NodeType with either), AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod is 0 to 35, ManualSnapshotRetentionPeriod is -1 or 1 to 3653, IpAddressType is ipv4 or dualstack, and MultiAZ is reported as Enabled or Disabled. At most 20 clusters exist per Region (a local limit that answers ClusterQuotaExceeded).

A cluster reports its parameter group (status in-sync), VPC security groups (status active) and IAM roles (status in-sync) by name or ID only and names its cluster subnet group, none of which needs to exist or is protected from deletion while in use; it reports no VPC, subnets or Availability Zones of its own, and DescribeClusters refuses TagKeys and TagValues.

Snapshot schedules, scheduled actions, usage limits, event subscriptions, HSM certificates and configurations, snapshot copy grants, authentication profiles and cluster security groups are not implemented: they need a cluster, a topic, a key, an IAM role or a schedule grammar the stored model cannot evaluate, so their APIs return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501.

Parameter values are not modeled: ModifyClusterParameterGroup, ResetClusterParameterGroup, DescribeClusterParameters and DescribeDefaultClusterParameters are not implemented, and default parameter groups and the default subnet group are not pre-created. A parameter group family is stored without checking that it exists. Parameter group names are 1 to 255 letters, digits or hyphens, start with a letter, contain no trailing or consecutive hyphens and are stored in lowercase.

A subnet group needs 1 to 20 distinct subnet-xxxxxxxx or subnet-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx IDs that are not resolved, so it reports no VPC, Availability Zone, subnet status, group status or supported IP address type; the 20-subnet limit is returned as ClusterSubnetQuotaExceededFault. Subnet group names are 1 to 255 letters, digits or hyphens, are stored in lowercase and must not be Default.

DescribeClusters, DescribeClusterParameterGroups and DescribeClusterSubnetGroups refuse TagKeys, TagValues and Marker values that were not issued for the request, accept MaxRecords from 20 to 100 and fail with the operation's not-found fault for an unknown name. Resource counts per Region (50 parameter groups, 50 subnet groups and 20 clusters) are local limits.

CreateTags, DeleteTags and DescribeTags apply to the three stored resource kinds by ARN (arn:aws:redshift:region:account:parametergroup:name, subnetgroup:name and cluster:id) and fail with ResourceNotFoundFault for a missing or out-of-region resource. DescribeTags requires one ResourceName ARN and filters its tags by TagKeys and TagValues; ResourceType, MaxRecords, Marker and account-wide tag enumeration are not supported. Tags also appear on group and cluster descriptions. Tag keys for writes are required and must not start with aws:. Removing a missing key succeeds.
